passes.title: PBC first-pass results
passes.summary_excerpt: Use the verified immutable public release as the research baseline. The historical old runtime is equivalent on the tested default-preset sets but is not source-identical. Current root is a combined trajectory/performance variant, not clean release PBC 3.0. No PBC 3.1 release success is established by this pass.

passes.title: PBC Pass 2 research summary
passes.summary_excerpt: All four workstreams completed locally. The pass establishes matched-work engineering speedups, screens the single-stage quality/resolution frontier, rejects two tested lossless entropy transformations, and confirms fixed runtime candidates on main/holdout. It does not authorize or enable a production PBC 3.1 configuration.

passes.summary_excerpt: The combined performance optimization and exact rectangle error-map reuse are confirmed local runtime improvements with identical output. Rate-aware allocation at 500k/35, weight 0.4, is a credible measured RD research lead that survives this holdout under interpolated existing-frontier comparisons. passes.title: Pass 9 completed on HF
passes.summary_excerpt: Yes: optimized PBC with explicit release RNG reproduces immutable PBC 3.0 exactly on HF in 100/100 image/preset cases (20 main, five holdout; all four presets). Complete file, decoded pixel and ordered patch hashes/counts, RGB MSE and final post-LZMA bpp agree. All 96 repeated timed release/restored comparisons also match.

passes.title: PBC 3.1 development baseline promotion
passes.summary_excerpt: Yes: `pbc31_release_rng_baseline` is now the default on the live HF demo, public compression/streaming paths and normal benchmark utilities. This is a development baseline, not an official PBC 3.1 release.

passes.title: PBC Pass 13 summary
passes.summary_excerpt: The frozen baseline remained unchanged. Work was limited to local research scripts, measurements, and reports.

passes.title: PBC Research Pass 14 summary
passes.summary_excerpt: Pass 14 completed the native runtime audit and prepared the standalone PBC 3.1 Python package. No rate-distortion experiment was run.

Across the 32 image/preset cases, encode time fell 34.00% and decode time fell 64.28%. passes.title: Pass 17 completed-file RD results
passes.summary_excerpt: The full-image DCT sidecar is promising on four of six images, but is not a production promotion. The current development codec remains pbc31_feature_histogram. Cat and Flower fail the studied rate range. Independent tile selection is rejected in its tested form. No alternative architecture or full-set confirmation was run.

passes.title: Pass 18 deterministic spatial proposals
passes.summary_excerpt: The tested contrast/binary-fit proposal generator did not identify a useful replacement for the ordinary chosen patch. It is rejected at frozen feasibility; this is a negative result for this one method, not proof that the stochastic search is optimal.

passes.title: Pass 19 summary
passes.summary_excerpt: The signed ternary hard-mask primitive failed the frozen feasibility gate. Stop after Phase A; no complete hybrid image files or completed-file results report were produced.

passes.title: Pass 20 multiscale completed-file results
passes.summary_excerpt: Stop after the fixed three-image screen. The prototype retains some ordinary-PBC RD wins but fails to improve the frozen Pass 17 frontier. Nine of twelve files are strictly dominated by frozen full-DCT files; the remaining three are dominated by the actual A-band repacks. No six-image extension, repeated candidate timing or activation rule follows.

passes.title: Pass 21 sparse hybrid completed files
passes.summary_excerpt: Sparse storage retains all four successful Pass17 ordinary-HQ dominance points with identical RGB pixels and much faster encoding. It solves the extreme-XZ encode bottleneck on this bounded screen. Full decoding remains too expensive for a general-purpose replacement; Cat/Flower remain RD failures.

passes.title: Pass 22 reconstruction results
passes.summary_excerpt: One sparse gather/IDCT/scatter method and one buffer-reuse method. No fused Numba kernel was implemented: compatible in-place NumPy/SciPy operations were sufficient to test the allocation hypothesis without changing color arithmetic. Frozen Pass21 remains the regression decoder; research_pass22.decoder.decode reads the identical P21S container through the unchanged split/read_coefficients functions.

passes.title: Pass 23 decoder-aware completed-file results
passes.summary_excerpt: The conservative target adjustment fails the frozen progression gate. It yields one same-preset strict RD win (Cat Quality), several HQ quality/rate trades, and two Quality points dominated by their unchanged controls. No Monet/Eiffel extension, three-repeat timing campaign, classifier, dual encode or parameter rescue followed.

passes.title: Pass 24 final-patch redundancy
passes.summary_excerpt: Stop at the completed-stream omission feasibility gate. Three strict RD improvements exist, but their final-file savings are only 14, 74 and 97 bytes. No sampled omission reaches 5% savings with at most 1% RGB MSE growth. This does not justify a pruning algorithm, cheap working-SSE predictor or integrated encoder experiment. Only this feasibility report and the summary are created; no postencode-pruning report.

passes.title: Pass 25 completed transform-base results
passes.summary_excerpt: Reject the tested architecture as a general-purpose improvement. Outcome C/D: useful initialization-only capacity does not produce a reliable completed-file RD gain with the existing patch policy, and conventional JPEG dominates 5 of 8 hybrid points. No extension or repeated timing campaign.

passes.title: Pass 26 handoff
passes.summary_excerpt: Both standalone Windows forms work. An optional exact C metric lowers six-case mean median encode time by 5.70% and reduces one Cat encode peak by about 147 MiB. Video-container correctness succeeds, temporal rate efficiency fails. Conventional controls do not support another incremental RD change.

passes.title: Pass 27 handoff
passes.summary_excerpt: PBC 3.2.0rc1 is a local engineering candidate, not a published release. Compression/model/presets/RNG/entropy/v0 format retain actual published 3.1 behavior.

passes.title: PBC 3.2.0 release acceptance
passes.summary_excerpt: Verdict: **READY WITH LIMITATIONS**. Mandatory functional, packaging, independent Windows and performance gates pass. Final 3.2.0 artifacts are local and await explicit publication approval. No release/tag/main/HF change was made.

passes.title: PBC V4: nonlocal grouping and seeded permutations
passes.summary_excerpt: Pass 29 is a bounded component study. It does not change the PBC codec or claim a V4 codec improvement.

passes.title: PBC V4 Pass 30: shared-action feasibility
passes.summary_excerpt: Phase A failed its stop gate. The four-pattern residual-shape fit cleared the 10% residual-SSE screen on only Cat, one of four content classes. Its 12.57% reduction beyond DC used all four patterns at multiple cells. The other classes reached 4.83% (Flower), 1.93% (Mario64) and 0.20% (Googlewiki). Phase B was not run: no enhancement streams, XZ sizes, rate-distortion points, or file-only decoder were built.

Local detail improves reconstruction when the stream is allowed to grow substantially. passes.title: PBC V4 â€” Pass 32: Rate-Aware Mode Selection and Generalization
passes.summary_excerpt: The fixed-grid predictive modes generalize to these three held-out photographs, but the gains are small and do not meet the screen for a meaningful improvement. R1 changes candidate ranking and yields additional measured frontier points, but it does not materially improve quality at a matched rate. Keep this as a research result; do not promote it as a release change.

passes.title: Pass 40 results
passes.summary_excerpt: The active Variance Boost path is confirmed. At equal qcolor, it lowers RGB MSE but spends more bytes; its rate penalty ranges from 5.7% to 216% in the PSNR component points. Rate calibration reverses that result: 9 of 10 delta-Q comparisons have worse RGB MSE than their delta-Q-off targets, with one effectively neutral. This does not support using the existing boost as a general equal-rate quality improvement.

passes.title: PBC V4 Pass 46 results
passes.summary_excerpt: This pass tested a narrowly defined question: can a compact source-resolution procedural stroke recover perceptually important detail at canonical PBC 3.1 Compression rates? It also rechecked canonical PBC output, compared two distinct AVIF quality-0 configurations, and added pinned AVIF points around PBC's measured rates. No codec architecture or stream was changed.

passes.title: Competitive status
passes.summary_excerpt: Pass 47 produced **no completed experimental PBC file and no demonstrated completed-file improvement** over canonical V3.1. The predeclared local gate failed its cross-image threshold, so the conditional continuation and selection-rule phases were not run. The oracle did find two large local RD-score alternatives, both on Mario64 Balanced; their effect after the remaining patch trajectory is unknown.
